prize_parts.citation: for transforming the measurement of intergenerational mobility and economic opportunity using population administrative data

statement.case_for: B018 remains my preferred achievement. The linked population-data programme made intergenerational mobility measurable at an unprecedented geographic and institutional resolution, created durable empirical infrastructure, and reshaped research on opportunity and inequality. Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman remain a defensible central group for this defined data-intensive mobility programme. Its maturity lies in more than a decade of extensive subsequent research and scrutiny, not in treating every later place-based result as settled.
statement.case_against: The programme joins measurement, descriptive geography, and causal work on childhood location, while important collaborators and earlier mobility scholars cannot all be recognized under a three-person limit. The available evidence does not justify a citation that treats observed geographic differences as a complete causal account of opportunity.

responses.point: Fredriksson argues that the population-scale mobility programme is mature, while cautioning that place-effect interpretation and three-person attribution remain difficult.
responses.response: I agree. The infrastructure and measurement contribution independently meet the threshold for recognition, whereas causal mechanisms and policy implications require greater restraint. This is why I have narrowed my citation from round 1: it no longer claims clarification of the causal role of place.

responses.point: Hassler favors B007's long-matured collateral and financial-amplification mechanisms and questions whether B018 is comparatively recent and whether place effects remain actively interpreted.
responses.response: B007 is a very strong alternative because of its longevity and conceptual reach. But its proposed configuration still joins collateral constraints with the financial accelerator and leaves Simon Gilchrist's position unresolved. B018 has an equally identifiable core when confined to mobility measurement and population-data infrastructure; this avoids relying on the still-active interpretation of place effects.

responses.point: Dreber Almenberg emphasizes that B018 should be centered on linked-data mobility measurement rather than the full range of place-effect claims.
responses.response: I concur. That distinction makes the achievement more coherent and renders Chetty, Hendren, and Friedman a more defensible allocation, though not an exhaustive account of the collaborative programme.

uncertainties: Whether Friedman is the most appropriate third laureate within the wider collaborative mobility-data programme.
Whether any final account of the achievement can distinguish its measurement infrastructure cleanly enough from subsequent causal research on childhood location.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile.
